provenance.source: THIN-SKIN-GUITAR-BUILD-ESTIMATE-1 sprint; all three components are engineering estimates with no owner-confirmation artifact.

notes: Burden ($0.09/hr) is an engineering estimate: ~$900 rack capital over a 7-year life at an assumed 1,500 occupancy-hours/year = 10,500 hours, giving $0.086/hr, rounded to $0.09. Not owner-confirmed.
Consumables ($0.02/hr) covers hangers and contact pads.
equipment_hour_rate ($0.12/hr) is a true-cost rate: burden 0.09 + electricity 0.01 + consumables 0.02. COST input, not a billing rate.

The rate is intentionally near-zero. Long cure occupancy is cheap in direct dollars and expensive in throughput and work-in-process; that trade is a scheduling and overhead question, not a direct-cost one, and is deferred to THIN-SKIN-BATCH-COSTING-1 and GUITAR-FULL-UNIT-COST-1.
Because floor space is charged as overhead rather than as a rack burden, this record understates the true cost of long cure cycles. Recheck once an overhead model exists.
